html_notes: Overall Direction The current 3D tablet-style design is not working. The team found it hard to read and felt that the way the layers from our platform graphic are laying down is confusing. The team also felt that it was not clearly enough a circle. The next version should be flat, centered, oriented so we're looking at it head-on and clearly communicate a flywheel effect. The pipe-style connectors between sections should be removed and instead we need to show a living, circular system where each section flows visibly into the next -- not just circular in concept but visually obvious as a loop. Structure & Flow The flywheel sits at the center and is the hero of the graphic. And we should keep the same ideas that we have right now where data flows in on one side, and outcomes flow out of the Activate layer on the other side. The circular motion between the internal layers should be immediately readable and we need to make sure our customers don't have to work to understand that it's a flywheel. The Inputs in the cloud section We want to have three buckets: Data Gold Mine / Business Context / Customer Preferences Sub-items for Version 1 only: Data Gold Mine: First party, Declarative, Engagement Business Context: Performance, Growth goals, KPIs Customer Preferences: User mix constraints, Strategic beliefs, Optimization guardrails Two Versions Required Version 1 — Text-heavy: Design a version of this graphic where we keep all of the text we currently have on screen, but we really simplify down the graphics -- maybe that's just showing one icon per section. Version 2 — More Visual: Just show the headlines of each step (Predict, Engineer, Activate, etc.) as labels flowing into the flywheel. Don't show any supporting text underneath the inputs in the cloud or underneath each headline. Clean and scannable, it should be designed for audiences who find dense graphics overwhelming. Im picturing a world where we can show Version 2 on screen during a call, and when we send an email to followup we share version 1 with the prospects so if they share it internally, the graphic is understandable to people who weren't on the call. I was thinking it could even look something like this where we add text to the right hand side to show the flow, but im open to ideas.
name: Marketecture flywheel graphic
notes:
Overall Direction
The current 3D tablet-style design is not working. The team found it hard to read and felt that the way the layers from our platform graphic are laying down is confusing. 
The team also felt that it was not clearly enough a circle. 
The next version should be flat, centered, oriented so we're looking at it head-on and clearly communicate a flywheel effect. 
The pipe-style connectors between sections should be removed and instead we need to show a living, circular system where each section flows visibly into the next -- not just circular in concept but visually obvious as a loop.

Structure & Flow
The flywheel sits at the center and is the hero of the graphic. And we should keep the same ideas that we have right now where data flows in on one side, and outcomes flow out of the Activate layer on the other side. 
The circular motion between the internal layers should be immediately readable and we need to make sure our customers don't have to work to understand that it's a flywheel.

The Inputs in the cloud section
We want to have three buckets: Data Gold Mine / Business Context / Customer Preferences

Sub-items for Version 1 only:
Data Gold Mine: First party, Declarative, Engagement
Business Context: Performance, Growth goals, KPIs
Customer Preferences: User mix constraints, Strategic beliefs, Optimization guardrails

Two Versions Required
Version 1 — Text-heavy: Design a version of this graphic where we keep all of the text we currently have on screen, but we really simplify down the graphics -- maybe that's just showing one icon per section.
Version 2 — More Visual: Just show the headlines of each step (Predict, Engineer, Activate, etc.) as labels flowing into the flywheel. Don't show any supporting text underneath the inputs in the cloud or underneath each headline. Clean and scannable, it should be designed for audiences who find dense graphics overwhelming.

Im picturing a world where we can show Version 2 on screen during a call, and when we send an email to followup we share version 1 with the prospects so if they share it internally, the graphic is understandable to people who weren't on the call. I was thinking it could even look something like this where we add text to the right hand side to show the flow, but im open to ideas.
